revision_summary: 1. Fix wrong_ts on rep_intent.evidence[0]: the quote 'Just wanted to confirm your address here...' is correctly attributed but timestamped 00:17 when it actually begins around 00:29-00:39 in the transcript. Correct the ts. 2. Reconsider the intro_legitimacy_omission framing: this call is a customer callback (rep's opening line 'Hey. This is Randy' precedes the visible transcript's customer response), not a fresh outbound lead — intros.standard doesn't cleanly apply to callback scenarios. Either note this as a schema gap (callback intro variant not yet defined) rather than scoring it as a clean omission, and adjust script_coverage.intro_legitimacy status from flat 'skipped' to reflect this ambiguity. 3. Add the missed lead-record data-quality moment at 02:39 (utility company listed as Rappahannock but customer corrects to Dominion) — this parallels the Tommy/Tony name mismatch already caught and should be merged into a single 'lead record integrity' theme in multi_touch_patterns and the handoff brief's unresolved_concerns. 4. Add the missed legitimacy-probe moment at 02:50 ('Who are you folks based out of') as its own classified moment (protocols-adjacent legitimacy check) rather than only using it as supporting evidence for the intro-omission point — the rep's answer was reasonably specific and deserves its own assessment. 5. Add the second vulnerability disclosure at 07:00 (retired, doctor-appointment-dependent schedule) to vulnerability_disclosure_handling coverage — schema explicitly lists health/retirement-related disclosures as a trigger category, and this one went unacknowledged by the rep, distinct from the tech-vulnerability already caught at 04:33. 6. Rename or reconcile the invented classification label 'unanchored_soft_exit' — it isn't a schema-defined term and shouldn't be presented as if pulled directly from the schema's directive list; either use plain descriptive language or map explicitly to the closest schema directive with a caveat that it's Stewart's own label.
